chunks: As for what Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad narrated from Dāwūd al-Ṣirmī, who said:

I asked Abā al-Ḥasan عليه السلام and said to him: I go out on this route, and sometimes there is no place in which I can perform salat except snow, so what should I do? He said: If it is possible for you not to perform sajdah upon the snow, then do not perform sajdah upon it; and if it is not possible for you, then level it and perform sajdah upon it.

So the bearing of this report concerns the state of necessity, according to what we have already presented in the first report, and what he also clarified in the report of Manṣūr ibn Ḥāzim, which we have already presented earlier.

key_terms.أَبَا الْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: Abā al-Ḥasan, the Imam عليه السلام being addressed in the narration
key_terms.الثَّلْجِ: snow, the surface discussed for performing sajdah
key_terms.الضَّرُورَةِ: necessity, the condition under which the concession applies
key_terms.تَسْجُدَ: to perform sajdah, the act of prostration in salat
key_terms.فَسَوِّهِ: level it, meaning to smooth or prepare the snow surface

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to perform sajdah on snow when no other place is available?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding performing sajdah on snow when a person cannot find another place for salat. The Imam عليه السلام states that sajdah on snow should be avoided if possible, but in a state of necessity one may level the snow and perform sajdah on it.
